The Autonomic Nervous System
TWO MAIN DIVISIONS: SYMPATHETIC AND PARASYMPATHETIC
NERVOUS SYSTEMS
• Link between the central nervous system (CNS) and
peripheral organs
• Automatically controls many systems in our body. To
different extent, it mainly regulates:
- Contraction and relaxation of vascular and visceral
smooth muscle
- All exocrine and certain endocrine secretions
- The heartbeat
- Energy metabolism (especially in the liver and skeletal
muscle)

Cholinergic receptors antagonists
ANTICHOLINERGICS / ANTIMUSCARINICS
nACh receptors antagonists
• Not clinically useful for ANS
• Muscle relaxants act on the neuromuscular junction
(E.g.: Pancuronium)
mACh receptors antagonists
• Also called parasympatholytic, antimuscarinic or
anticholinergic drugs because they compete and block
the action of ACh at the muscarinic receptors.
• Examples: Hyoscine (Scopolamine) butylbromide
(Buscopan) or hydrobromide (Travacalm), atropine and
Tiotropium (Spiriva - COPD)
